summary: Extended the policy decoder with HTML-tokenizer numeric termination: an optional x/X prefix selects hexadecimal, the longest decimal or hex digit run is consumed, and a trailing semicolon is optional. Decimal &#106avascript:, zero-padded decimal, terminated decimal/hex and uppercase-X forms now lose the URI attribute. Forms resolving to an allowed scheme or a relative reference keep their existing bytes, and a hex run that consumes the leading a is correctly not the javascript scheme. Invalid, zero and surrogate code points are left untouched for the policy view so malformed controls keep their bytes; a browser maps them to a replacement character and cannot form a scheme from them. The full local suite passed (256 tests, 2 expected failures), including 22 focused entity-URI checks. Evidence strength: direct local result plus parser-semantics controls. Limitation: the official evaluator remains external.
next_hint: Run one consolidated end-to-end matrix that re-parses every emitted URI attribute with the same HTML parser, and apply only the source delta to a fresh copy before exporting the official patch JSONL.
